citation.sourceDocument: Utah Code §59-10-104 as amended by SB 60 (2026 session, signed 2026-03-23): 4.45% flat individual income tax for tax years beginning on or after 2026-01-01
citation.sourceNote: SB 60 (signed 2026-03-23) cut the 2025 rate of 4.5% to 4.45% for tax years beginning on or after 2026-01-01, amending Utah Code §59-10-104 — the enrolled bill reads "(b) 4.45%" over a struck "[(b) 4.5%.]". Verified against the enrolled bill on 2026-08-29, because the Tax Commission's own pages have not caught up: its rate schedule's newest row still reads "January 1, 2025 - current, 4.5%" and the line-by-line instructions still say "multiply line 9 by 4.5 percent". The 4.45% here is the law; 4.5% is the agency's website lagging it. Utah has no standard deduction — it taxes federal AGI directly and grants relief through the nonrefundable taxpayer tax credit (Utah Code §59-10-1018): 6% of the federal deduction, reduced by 1.3% of taxable income above a filing-status base ($18,213 single/MFS, $27,320 HoH, $36,426 MFJ/QSS), at the most recent published (2025) base amounts pending the 2026-indexed figures. The $2,111-per-dependent personal exemption that would enlarge the credit base is omitted (the engine models the no-dependent filer, like every other state), so the figure errs slightly high — the conservative side for setting money aside.
